interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. VerifyLeader reports success although the leader can reach fewer voters than the voter quorum it sized, because acknowledgements arriving on non-voter replication streams are counted as support. Evidence from receipt 7a54f3754b0b423aaf1ba6c0365367c0 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0). Parsed index 1, the trigger: five members were bootstrapped, two were demoted to non-voters, and the leader's transport was disconnected in both directions from the two remaining voters, so voters_reachable=1 against quorum_voters=2 while nonvoters_reachable=2; VerifyLeader completed with verify_ok=true and an empty error, and the node was still Leader. Parsed index 3, the control on an identically built cluster with the non-voters also disconnected (nonvoters_reachable=0): the same call completed with verify_ok=false and the error 'leadership lost while committing log', the node by then a Follower. The two cases differ only in whether the non-voters could answer, so the successful verification in the trigger is attributable to non-voter acknowledgements rather than to voter support. Mechanism from source: verifyLeader sets quorumSize with quorumSize(), which counts only voters (raft.go:1087-1100), but registers the verify future on every entry of leaderState.replState (raft.go:966-990), and startStopReplication creates a replication state for every configured server including non-voters (raft.go:583-600); any successful heartbeat or AppendEntries response calls notifyAll(true) (replication.go:100-112), which increments the verify future's vote count (future.go:274-293) and completes it at the voter-sized quorum. The library already uses the correct supporter set one function away: checkLeaderLease iterates the latest configuration and counts only voters (raft.go:1037-1050), so the two paths disagree about who can establish leadership. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a client that calls VerifyLeader to protect a read (api.go:927-931) is told the leader still holds a voter quorum while it can reach none of the other voters, so the guard against serving stale reads after leadership loss does not hold in a cluster that contains non-voters. A successor run, receipt e49121154f514e39b6c1a37a2c353a4a, repeated the call every 50 ms after the first verification and quantified the window: parsed index 1 again records verify_ok=true for the partitioned leader, and parsed index 2 records loop_successes=20 with ms_until_failure=1015 before the node became a Follower, so twenty separate verifications succeeded across about one second; the control at parsed index 4 recorded verify_ok=false and parsed index 5 recorded loop_successes=0 with failure at 0 ms. The false assurance therefore lasts for the leader lease interval (LeaderLeaseTimeout, one second in this harness), not for a single call. A clean-copy repeat of the same fixed experiment, receipt 13b7844febba4a6d80c7331818c943f6, reproduced the window: parsed index 1 verify_ok=true, parsed index 2 loop_successes=20 with ms_until_failure=1014, parsed index 4 verify_ok=false and parsed index 5 loop_successes=0. Both runs therefore agree on the count and on a window of about one second at this lease setting.

knowledge.assertion: VerifyLeader sizes a voter quorum but registers the verification on every replication stream, including non-voters, whose acks increment its vote count.
checkLeaderLease counts only voters, unlike VerifyLeader.

counterevidence: The verification returned before the lease check stepped the leader down, so the false success is bounded by the leader lease interval rather than permanent; in the control that same step-down produced the error the trigger avoided.
VerifyLeader returning nil installed no leader and returned no data; the harm requires a client to rely on it as the guard the documentation describes, and this harness issued no reads.

Non-voter reachability does show the leader is alive and connected, so a deployment that used VerifyLeader only as a liveness probe would not be affected; the code sizes a voter quorum, which makes quorum the stated intent.
The partition was modelled by removing in-memory transport routing in both directions between the leader and the voters, not by dropping packets or crashing members.
limitations: One configuration shape was exercised: three voters and two non-voters, with the leader cut from both other voters. Other suffrage mixes, a single non-voter, or a non-voter whose heartbeat is the only one in flight were not tested.

The exposure window was measured only at one lease setting: with LeaderLeaseTimeout of one second the partitioned leader returned twenty successful verifications over about 1,015 ms and, in a clean-copy repeat, twenty over about 1,014 ms before stepping down, so the window tracks the configured lease but was not varied.
No client reads were issued, so the end-to-end stale-read consequence is inferred from the documented purpose of VerifyLeader rather than observed.
The demotions completed before the partition, but each member's view of the new configuration was not read back before the transport was cut.

An attempt to observe the end-to-end stale read (majority commits a newer value while the partitioned leader verifies) did not succeed in construction: once the leader is cut from the voters it steps down at its next lease check, and forcing the majority side to campaign immediately still left the partitioned node a Follower by the time the new value had committed, so a positive verification concurrent with an already-stale FSM was not captured. Whether the two windows can be aligned in practice, and how wide the intersection is, remains unsettled.
